svg.title: Type-I products, finite matrix corners and invariant transfer
svg.desc: Countably many separably represented type-I legs may have infinite dimension and nonfaithful states. Finite positive spectral selections retain mass at least three quarters. Their full corner is a faithful finite-matrix product. Corner invariants agree with those of the original factor, and summably small deleted word masses preserve positive block witnesses.

g.text: From general type-I legs to finite matrix coordinates
Countably many separably represented legs; infinite dimensions and density kernels are allowed.
The product state may be nonfaithful.
qₙⱼ = pₙⱼ / cₙ for j in Jₙ
Choose finite positive spectral sets Jₙ with cₙ = Σⱼ∈Jₙ pₙⱼ > 1 − εₙ
The corner map need not be an isomorphism M ≅ eMe. The projection e need not be finite in M.
Type III comparison or a semifinite trace.
Keep pairs with both words in J_I.
Ratios agree: p_I = C_I q_I on selected words.
Disjoint blocks give finite total loss when ratios ≥ a > 0.
For r > 0, r ≠ 1: intrinsic spectrum ⇔ original eigenvalue block witnesses.
For 0 < λ < 1: M ⊗ Rλ ≅ Rλ ⇔ 2π / |log λ| belongs to T(M).
Proofs: Sections 29–32. The two endpoints 0 and 1 of the block test are treated separately in the text.
